summary: Stream resume randomizes chunk ordering, causing silent truncation of closing bullet lists
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that after an SSE reconnect sequence the final portion of streamed responses containing closing bulleted lists is often missing without an explicit error. The stream resumes and client receives later token fragments, but the concluding list items are truncated or never emitted.

Impact: Multiple production customers (NoteFlo) observe truncated bullets in generated documents which removes action items for end-users. This is causing content integrity problems and increased support load.

Environment: Production, hosted API in us-east; traffic passes through customer's corporate reverse proxy and our edge ALB. Issue observed primarily on long responses (>1,200 tokens) with intermittent network path changes.

Observed behavior: When client experiences a short disconnect and issues a resume/continue request, we sometimes deliver chunks in non-monotonic order; terminal bullet items are absent and no 5xx is returned. Resume finishes normally from the client perspective (stream closed) but content is missing.

Expected behavior: After reconnect/resume the SSE sequence should reconstitute an identical token stream including final bullets and termination marker.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a generate request producing >1,000 tokens with bulleted list near the end (templates supplied by customer).
2) During stream delivery trigger a short TCP path change (simulate NAT rebind or corporate proxy reset).
3) Client issues resume request with last-known offset.
4) Observe final bullets missing from assembled stream though final close event is received.
logs: Edge logs (us-east ALB) show 200 OK for initial connection, then 101/keepalive events; resume handshake shows matching resume_token but sequence numbers logged on our edge are sometimes out of order: seq: 1140, 1141, 1139. Upstream worker (pod-serve-12) logs indicate chunk flush order 'ok' but downstream TCP timestamps show reorder during proxy handoff. No application-level exceptions. See attached snippets in related_github_prs.
comments: Support (Alejandra): Collected reproducible curl-based recipe from customer and confirmed truncation on our prod cluster. Customer provided packet capture showing midstream FIN+RST from corporate proxy.

SRE (Ravi): Replayed traffic in staging with same proxy repro; observed reorder at HTTP/2 multiplexing layer on ALB. Edge sometimes re-emits buffered frames after a connection migration which can interleave resumed chunks. Filing with infra and serving-runtime teams.
Customer (NoteFlo): Impacting scheduled meeting notes export; requested ETA and asked for a temporary mitigation to avoid data loss while we investigate.

Engineering (J. Lin): Hypothesis: resume token acceptance path doesn't enforce strictly monotonic delivery of buffered fragments on connection migration. Need to add an ordering guard and stronger sequence validation on resume acceptance.
investigation_notes: 1) Reproduced with an instrumented client behind a controlled proxy that intentionally reorders TLS fragments. Truncation correlates with non-monotonic seq numbers during resume handshake.
2) Edge ALB uses HTTP/2 multiplexing and will replay buffered frames after graceful teardown; replay window can overlap with resume window causing duplicates and out-of-order application frames.
3) Serving runtime currently relies on resume_token + offset but does not atomically validate finalization markers when sequence reordering is detected.

4) KV cache priming and prefix cache application appears resilient; missing content is not in cache, suggesting the final tokens were never assembled into the outgoing stream due to order-drop in our stitcher.
5) Short-term mitigation tested: enable strict single-stream affinity on edge for the affected customer and force drain rather than replay; this reduces occurrence in canary tests.
resolution_summary:
Workaround: Enabled 'preserve-chunk-order' routing for NoteFlo on us-east edge (config change applied 2026-03-11) which prevented further truncation for the customer.

Fix implemented: Added sequence-number validation and idempotent-append logic to stream stitcher to reject out-of-order fragments on resume and to request retransmit of missing ranges. Patch merged: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5772. Deployed to staging 2026-03-11 and rolled to prod canary 2026-03-12.

Follow-ups: 1) Add automated test harness that simulates proxy-induced reorder (INC-2026-03-reorder-test). 2) Review ALB replay settings with infra and document recommended customer-side proxy behaviors. 3) Notify affected customers and recommend enabling our keepalive-affinity flag if they route through aggressive middleboxes.
